result: The LIN-12/Notch signaling pathway specifies vm2 as the postsynaptic target through cell-autonomous activation in vm2 by APX-1/Delta expressed in surrounding cells (secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1). This pathway functions at the L4 stage, independent of earlier developmental roles, and involves canonical signaling through SEL-12/Presenilin and LAG-1/CSL transcription factor. The pathway includes positive feedback through LAG-1 binding sites in the lin-12 promoter.

result: LIN-12/Notch signaling up-regulates UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 expression in vm2 at the transcriptional level through LAG-1 binding sites in their regulatory regions. UNC-40, potentiated by MADD-2, is both necessary and sufficient for muscle arm formation and responds to environmental cues to guide muscle arm extension. The two genes function partly in parallel pathways with UNC-40 playing the deterministic role.

result: HSN and VC4/5 neurons form synapses exclusively on vm2 muscle cells, with presynaptic specializations juxtaposed to postsynaptic muscle arms enriched in UNC-103E. Pre- and postsynaptic specializations develop at different times (HSN presynaptic at early L4, muscle arms 5-6 hours later) and independently of each other.

result: Vulval epithelial cells, rather than presynaptic neurons, organize postsynaptic development in the egg-laying circuit. Primary vulval epithelial cells guide HSN presynaptic development through SYG-1/SYG-2 interaction, while secondary vulval epithelial cells guide postsynaptic muscle arm development through APX-1/LIN-12 signaling. Muscle arms grow along the interface between primary and secondary epithelial cells, possibly responding to membrane-associated or locally secreted cues.

The model of epithelial cells as organizers is well-supported (C49, C91).

result: Partial loss-of-function alleles of LIN-12/Notch pathway components (lin-12(wy750), apx-1(wy755), sel-12(wy760)) specifically disrupt vm2 muscle arm development without affecting vulval morphogenesis or general muscle development, suggesting muscle arm development requires higher LIN-12/Notch signaling activity. These mutants show functional defects in egg-laying behavior due to asynchronous Ca2+ transients in vulval muscles.

result: Temperature-shift experiments with lin-12(n676n930) demonstrate that LIN-12/Notch signaling functions at the L4 stage to specify vm2 postsynaptic identity, with more than 80% of animals shifted to restrictive temperature at mid-L4 still showing muscle arm defects, indicating a late developmental requirement distinct from earlier roles in vulval morphogenesis.

This is consistent with the differential sensitivity model where muscle arm development requires higher signaling activity (C18).

result: Background information establishes that UNC-40/DCC is the C. elegans homolog of vertebrate DCC/neogenin receptors for Netrin, previously shown to regulate body wall muscle arm formation, and that vulval muscles derive from the postembryonic M lineage through three rounds of cell division.
